title: Active Custom Element Constructor Map does not solve re-entrancy due to early removal

labels.name: topic: custom elements
labels.description: Relates to custom elements (as defined in DOM and HTML)

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

When implementing the "active custom element constructor map", to ensure that registries resolve correctly during reentrant HTML Construction, the spec mandates we remove the surrounding agent's element constructor entry early, which causes re-entry via upgrade to fail.

The relevant spec is [HTML element constructors](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#html-element-constructors), step 3:

> 
> 3. If the surrounding agent's active custom element constructor mapNewTarget exists:
>    1. Set registry to the surrounding agent's active custom element constructor mapNewTarget.
>   2. Remove the surrounding agent's active custom element constructor mapNewTarget.
> 4. Otherwise, set registry to the current global object's associated Document's custom element registry.

Removing at step 3.2 means that a reentrant invocation of the same constructor during an upgrade no longer finds the entry, so it falls through to step 4 and resolves registry to the global Document's registry instead of the scoped registry that the upgrade was using. When the same constructor is registered in both a scoped registry and the global registry (under different local names), the reentrant new then resolves a different definition whose construction stack is empty. So it falls through step 9 (empty construction stack) path and produces a fresh, valid element, instead of hitting the "already constructed marker" TypeError that the reentrancy guard is supposed to raise.

Deleting the line (as in, not removing said entry) causes these tests to pass. I suppose there is a potential risk that the map now contains stale entries - I need to dig further to see how true this is though.

This seems to be borne out by looking at respective engines; AIUI Chrome and WebKit do _not_ implement the "active custom element constructor map", only Ladybird does and the results are that [Ladybird fails the rentry tests](https://wpt.fyi/results/custom-elements/registries/constructor-reentry-with-different-definition.html?label=master&label=experimental&product=chrome&product=ladybird&product=firefox&product=safari&aligned&view=interop&q=label%3Ainterop-2026-scoped-custom-element-registries).

I'm trying to implement this in Firefox and I'm uncovering the same issue.

Blink has separate map; the definition carried on a per-window/constructor construction stack, which can be inspected during the the whole scope ([v8_html_constructor.cc](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/bindings/core/v8/v8_html_constructor.cc), [custom_element_construction_stack.cc](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/custom/custom_element_construction_stack.cc)).

WebKit has a single Document::activeCustomElementRegistry slot, save/restored around the constructor call, but it's not restored until construct returns ([JSCustomElementInterface.cpp](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/bindings/js/JSCustomElementInterface.cpp), [JSHTMLElementCustom.cpp](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/bindings/js/JSHTMLElementCustom.cpp)).

I think this can be resolved by removing the `Remove...` line and instead leaving it to callsites to remove it, post construction.
